correctness.rationale: The published definition gives \(3^4=81\) vertices. The verifier reconstructs the undirected loop-free overlap graph and obtains exactly \(237\) edges, checks an explicit proper \(3\)-colouring on every edge, and verifies a triangle on vertices \(0000,0001,1000\). Thus \(\chi(S(4,3))=3\) exactly. Huang--Kitaev--Pyatkin state that every \(3\)-colourable graph is word-representable, so the consequence is valid without a search for a representing word.

evidence: Petyuk proves word-representability only for \(S(n,2)\) and non-word-representability for \(S(2,k)\) and \(S(3,k)\), then conjectures non-word-representability for \(n\ge4,k\ge3\).

Huang--Kitaev--Pyatkin restate the same conjecture and prove positive results for induced subgraphs \(S_m(n,k)\); their full-graph conjecture remains stated, so those theorems do not dominate the claim.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The later induced-subgraph theorems do not imply word-representability of the full graph \(S(4,3)\). Conversely, a positive result for the full graph directly contradicts the conjecture rather than being a routine special case of the published positive families.
